status_on_pages: open on the pages; letter explicitly says little has been proved
computation: No computation replaces existence or a specified duality morphism
fate: ACMV2023 Theorems6.1,7.1,7.9 and9.5 give existence/endpoints and the characteristic-zero comparison with algebraic intermediate Jacobians in i=1,2,n. Ottem–Suzuki2020 Corollary4.2, p.9, shows that the usual Abel–Jacobi target need not itself be universal in codimension3 even when a representative exists. Kahn2021 Conjecture1 exhibits an explicit higher-codimension nonexistence expectation, not a proved counterexample.
fate_date: Picard/Albanese known before1964; Murre1985; Ottem–Suzuki first2019/published2020; ACMV2019/2023
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Partly developed; no all-codimension existence/duality theorem matching the full programme was found. The integral Abel–Jacobi identification has a known failure in higher codimension.

statement: The symmetric divisor correspondence obtained from intersections of middle-codimension families is hoped to descend to a positive polarization on the proposed abelian quotient. Symmetry and nondegeneracy only produce a symmetric isogeny to the dual; ampleness is an additional requirement. The page itself notes that primitive decomposition must be taken into account.
status_on_pages: open on the pages; sign and primitive qualifications are explicitly unsettled
computation: computations.md §13 distinguishes symmetric isogeny from polarization and records the missing primitive/sign conventions
fate: Grothendieck1969 pp.194–197 and Kleiman1968 §§3.2–3.3 formulate primitive Hodge-type positivity. ACMV2025 Theorem12.6, pp.66–67, constructs a symmetric morphism/isogeny with explicit Bloch-map and Tate-module hypotheses. Theorem12.12(3), p.68, gives a distinguished symmetric isomorphism for a smooth projective threefold over a perfect field with universally trivial CH0; over a subfield of C its negative agrees with the principal Hodge polarization. Chapter13, p.71 onward, requires lifting/specialization hypotheses to prove polarization in positive characteristic. These exact statements were opened; no all-codimension unconditional positivity theorem is inferred.
fate_date: Classical Hodge positivity; Grothendieck1969; specified algebraic-representative advances2025
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Partly developed; general algebraic positivity in positive characteristic remains conjectural. No proof of ampleness is extracted from a symmetric correspondence alone.

statement: For a pencil of hyperplane sections with geometrically integral fibres and generic fibre Y, the programme compares the Néron–Tate pairing of restricted algebraically trivial cycles of complementary codimensions i+j=dimY+1 with an intersection on the total space. The literal formula still lacks a uniform meaning of m outside the middle case and a specification of vertical corrections/admissible lifts.
status_on_pages: open on the pages; a more general fibration statement and local variant are requested
computation: computations.md §13 checks codimension: i+j=n=dimY+1; no unjustified numerical height calculation is claimed
fate: Kahn2024 Refined height pairing, Theorem4.14 in accepted version p.31, constructs a pairing on admissible subgroups over function fields, with coefficients inverting the exponential characteristic; Theorem5.6 includes algebraically trivial cycles and Theorem5.10 records an explicit negative-sign comparison for elliptic curves. Künnemann2001 Theorem1.6/Corollary1.7 constructs heights for all abelian varieties over number fields via lifts orthogonal to vertical cycles. Neither source validates the leaf’s unqualified sign/normalization.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: A substantial general height theory exists, but the precise pencil identity needs admissible lifts and fixed signs; it is not proved merely by the formal intersection number.

statement: For the proposed P^i, restriction to a generic hyperplane section Y of n-dimensional X is predicted to be an isomorphism if2i≤n−1, to identify the fixed part if2i=n, and to be surjective if2i≥n+1. The deleted finite-kernel assertion is not retained. These are assertions about the proposed cycle representatives, not just ordinary cohomology.
status_on_pages: open on the pages with a deleted stronger assertion
computation: computations.md §13 compares the degree2i−1 thresholds with weak Lefschetz and records why the cycle quotient is extra data
fate: Katz–Messing1974 Corollary(Ogus), p.76, gives weak Lefschetz for their reasonable cohomologies; ACMV2023 Theorems7.1,7.9,9.5 identify actual representatives in endpoint/codimension2 cases. Their combination does not prove the all-i quotient statement. Searches of modern algebraic-representative literature did not locate the exact all-codimension formulation.
fate_date: Classical weak Lefschetz; Katz–Messing received8August1973/published1974; representative theory1985–2023
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Conditional programme beyond its known endpoint/specified representative cases. The fixed-part and surjectivity assertions require exact quotient and lattice conventions.

statement: If τ-equivalence means that a nonzero integer multiple is algebraically equivalent to zero, numerical equivalence equals τ-equivalence for divisors (Matsusaka). The same assertion for every algebraic cycle on a smooth projective variety is false: a very general complex quintic threefold has non-torsion homologically trivial codimension2 cycles modulo algebraic equivalence, hence numerically trivial cycles that are not τ-trivial.
status_on_pages: stated without proof as Th.7, with a Matsusaka marginal attribution
computation: computations.md §13: homologically trivial implies numerically trivial, while nonzero rational Griffiths group rules out τ-triviality
fate: Clemens1983 Theorem0.2 and Corollary0.3, pp.19–20, prove an infinite-dimensional rational Abel–Jacobi image and non-finite generation modulo algebraic equivalence for very general quintic threefolds. Kahn2024 Theorem5.6 explicitly uses Matsusaka only for divisors. The definition of τ is reconstructed and must be checked elsewhere before attributing a literal counterexample to an undefined notation.
fate_date: Matsusaka divisor theorem before1964; Griffiths earlier counterexamples; strongerClemens1983
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: False in all codimensions under the standard τ meaning; true divisor case retained. If τ meant another relation, the manuscript statement is not identifiable without its definition.

statement: The letter first predicts a subquotient realization of T_ℓJ^i in H^(2i−1)(X,Z_ℓ(i)), then hopes for an injection. Modern constructions give a rational realization and, for i=1,2,n, injections after controlling miniversal-cycle denominators; a canonical integral inclusion in codimension2 requires stronger torsion comparison. Arbitrary all-i integral embeddings are not supplied.
status_on_pages: open on the pages, distinguishing the weaker subquotient from the stronger embedding
computation: computations.md §13 records the multiplier r and why ℓ∤r matters
fate: ACMV2023 Proposition8.2, p.31, proves the injection for i=1,2,n and ℓ different from the characteristic and coprime to the miniversal multiplier r, with torsion removed from the cohomology target. ACMV2025 Proposition10.3, pp.50–51, proves the canonical torsion/Tate comparison in characteristic0 or under a cohomological diagonal-decomposition hypothesis; Definition10.5, p.52, keeps the general positive-characteristic condition explicit.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Partly established with exact codimension, characteristic, torsion and denominator hypotheses. It is not an unconditional all-codimension canonical Z_ℓ embedding.

statement: In characteristic0 the letter predicts a tangent-space inclusion into the Hodge piece H^i(X,Ω_X^(i−1)). For the algebraic part of an intermediate Jacobian, its level-one Hodge substructure gives the corresponding tangent realization, with a choice of covariant/contravariant and duality conventions; it does not identify a tangent space for an as-yet-unconstructed all-i representative.
status_on_pages: open on the pages; conjectural margin
computation: computations.md §13 checks Hodge bidegree(i−1,i) and distinguishes Lie space from its dual
fate: ACMV2023 §9 and Theorems9.1,9.3,9.5 construct/descent the algebraic intermediate Jacobian over subfields of C and compare it with representatives in i=1,2,n. These exact results support the level-one Hodge realization, not the asserted integral equality or a positive-characteristic Hodge analogue.
fate_date: Classical intermediate-Jacobian theory; precise descent/relative results2019–2023
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Established for the specified algebraic intermediate-Jacobian object after variance is fixed; the general manuscript quotient remains conjectural.

statement: For a noetherian nonnegatively graded ring with an adic degree filtration, completion is flat and is exact on finite modules; for finitely generated graded modules it identifies with the product of homogeneous pieces. Faithfulness of completion on all modules needs an additional Jacobson-ideal condition; the margin instead restricts to graded modules satisfying the undefined condition TF.
status_on_pages: bulk argument cancelled; exactness/faithfulness retained only for the stated graded TF subcategory
computation: computations.md §12 proves the finite graded product description and explains why A/(x−1) is not a counterexample inside a graded subcategory
fate: Stacks00MB Lemma10.97.2 proves noetherian completion flatness/exactness on finite modules; Stacks00MC Lemma10.97.3 gives faithful flatness for I⊂Jac(A). These precise results settle the ordinary completion inputs but do not define the manuscript TF condition.
fate_date: Classical completion theory before/aroundthe manuscript; exact current sources checked2026
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Established finite graded statement. The broader TF claim remains unidentifiable without its definition; cancellation does not authorize an unrestricted version.

statement: For a finite spanning reduced root configuration in a rational vector space, a reflection preserving the roots and reversing a given root is orthogonal for the invariant positive form obtained by summing squared evaluations over the roots on the dual space. This determines the reflection uniquely. Integral coroot coefficients additionally use the root-lattice and crystallographic/primitive-root argument, not just positivity of a form.
status_on_pages: cancelled root-system draft with a proof sketch
computation: computations.md §12 proves positivity, invariance and uniqueness; keeps the integral-lattice argument separate
fate: SGA3XXI Lemma1.2.1 and Corollaries1.2.3–1.2.8, reedition pp.65–66, give the canonical sum-of-squares form and finiteness in root-data language. The exact lattice claim is compared with Definition1.1.1; root-lattice assumptions on the leaf are narrower than an arbitrary reductive root datum.
fate_date: Classical root theory; SGA3publication1970, exact reedition opened2026
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Established finite root-system construction with its hypotheses; this is external root-data material, not a motivic positivity result.

statement: The draft packages roots and coroots in two integral lattices with rationally perfect pairing, paired roots having value2 and the two reflections preserving their respective root sets. The two lattices are generated by roots and coroots here; this is not automatically the same as a perfect integral character/cocharacter pairing for every reductive group.
status_on_pages: cancelled definition with the essential value2 added in the margin
computation: computations.md §12 checks transpose reflections and distinguishes rational from integral perfectness
fate: SGA3XXI Definition1.1.1, Lemma1.1.4 and Corollary1.1.5, pp.63–64, state root data and their duality with explicit dual lattices. The published concept is a close developed counterpart; the broader integral lattice conventions are a genuine change of scope.
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Developed in the published root-datum theory, with the pairing distinction recorded rather than silently identifying the two definitions.

The current second-pass reading π_i supersedes the original transcription π_1. The mathematical surface statement is established; the exact historical claim about that paper is separately qualified.
